newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro bourses score new records, gold slips.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro bourses score new records, gold slips.

text.p: Key European stock markets, boosted by Wall Street's confident performance, showed the stamina to break more records in early business on Wednesday.
Hoping that the medicine of higher interest rates would not be needed just yet, London, Frankfurt, Paris and several other bourses moved up smartly into uncharted territory.
But unexpectedly strong British economic data, showing a marked drop in the jobless total, jangled a few nerves and trimmed share gains in London, Europe's busiest stock market.
"Everybody is now saying a rate rise is not going to happen but I don't think it's quite as clear cut as that," one London share trader said.
Gold, at 3-1/4 year lows below $353 an ounce, was down around $5 from overnight levels after investment funds took flight from the bullion market in New York.
Monday's news that the Dutch central bank had sold 300 tonnes of gold continues to hang over the market, analysts said.
"We may see a minor bounce but overall the market is firmly locked in a downside move...most people are looking to sell, while few are willing to buy," a bullion trader said.

On the currency market, the dollar held firm against the mark and yen. Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse on Tuesday said the mark could weaken ahead of European monetary union as some investors switched into other currencies. He added that he was opposed to a reduction in Germany's discount rate.
"I think Hesse's comments last night were very significant, suggesting the Bundesbank could keep interest rates low for some considerable time," DKB International chief economist Gerard Lyons said.
"It seems there isn't very much around to move the dollar today. But seeing that the dollar's come up very quickly, there's some danger of profit-taking," one dealer cautioned.
Japanese markets, which have provided plenty of interest for those elsewhere recently, were closed for a holiday.

The London stock market, where the value of blue chips in the FTSE 100 index had added 111 points or about 18.8 billion pounds ($31.4 billion) in the week's two previous sessions, rose at the start but slipped back after the jobless figures.

British unemployment fell 45,100 in December to 1.88 million to take the jobless rate down to 6.7 percent. Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke meets Eddie George, the Governor of the Bank of England, from 1500 GMT to discuss monetary policy.

The balance of market opinion seemed to be against an increase in interest rates from 6.0 percent just yet but the pound rose half a pfenning to 2.6710 marks after the jobs figures were seen to increase the chances of a rate rise.

In Frankfurt, Germany's blue-chip DAX index was closing in on the 3,000-point level after hitting a new all-time high in early bourse dealings -- although much of the gain had taken place in after-hours computerised trade on Tuesday.
Boosted by a general market boom, Tuesday's benign U.S. consumer prices report and the dollar's rally, the DAX gained 42.98 points, or 1.5 percent, to 2,991.96 within minutes.

Chemical shares and other dollar-sensitive stocks were the stars. "A dollar at this level is going to mean windfall profits for a lot of companies and we will see that reflected in earnings statements at the year end," said one dealer.

The French stock market also pushed to new highs at the opening, spurred by the advance on Wall Street and higher bonds. Belgium's Bel-20 blue-chip index scored a record high, too, in early business and Stockholm, Zurich and Athens scaled new peaks.

A dozen European bourses had hit all-time highs on Tuesday and Wall Street also set another record as long-term bond interest rates fell on economic news that eased inflation fears and amid optimism on company earnings.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended 53.11 points higher at 6,762.29 after being up around 45 as London markets closed.
CURRENCIES AT 1030 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 117.35 yen and 1.5965 marks, compared with 116.92 and 1.5957 late in Europe on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1030 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of key British stocks was 5.0 points or 0.12 percent higher at 4,179.8 but below an earlier record level of 4,191.5.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index was up 44.77 points, or 1.52 percent, at 2,993.65, in floor trade while the IBIS DAX index for electronica trade was up around 15 points.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 14.37 points, or 0.60 percent, higher at 2,416.51.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold slid to a morning fix of $352.45 an ounce, its lowest setting since October 4, 1993, from the previous London close of $357.55. Silver slipped five cents to $4.66.
